clue.text: Long story shows eastern prince in odd places

indicators.note: taking the letters in the first, third and fifth positions of the word prince

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale features a prince from the East, turning up in unlikely locations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in odd places' picks P, I and C from 'prince', which follow E.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem or saga, a lengthy tale of heroic deeds.

clue.text: Priest-king right to admit to trouble with gospel writer

indicators.note: the word for trouble lets the letter for right in, so it sits inside

parts.note: to pester someone is to trouble or bother them
John wrote the fourth Gospel

explanation.surface: A priest-king lets a right-hand man in, to the annoyance of an evangelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to admit' puts R inside PESTER, giving PRESTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Prester John was a legendary Christian priest and monarch said in medieval lore to rule in Asia or Africa.

clue.text: Damaged pectoral area does for tragic royal

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: An injury to the chest region finishes off a doomed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaged' rearranges PECTORAL plus A; 'does for' is a link meaning 'serves as'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleopatra, last ruler of Ptolemaic Egypt, died by suicide, making her the archetypal doomed queen of Shakespearean tragedy.

clue.text: Tourist attraction's sponsors coming around initially financing everything

indicators.note: the word for sponsors encircles the other pieces

parts.note: angels are backers who finance theatrical productions

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of financing

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Backers of a visitor site gather round, with funding at the start covering it all.
explanation.walkthrough: Angels are theatre backers. 'coming around' and 'initially' are the indicators; the 's after the definition is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Angel Falls in Venezuela is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, a major sightseeing destination.

clue.text: Freak indeed eating no food — appetite ultimately lost

indicators.note: the word for indeed takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: ay is an old or dialect word for yes, indeed

indicators.note: a letter goes missing from the word for food

parts.note: a meal is food

indicators.note: takes just the final letter of appetite

explanation.surface: Something odd: someone eating nothing, their hunger finally gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'indeed' is the archaic yes; 'ultimately' picks E, which 'lost' takes away, and 'eating' wraps the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A freak is an abnormality or aberration, something deviating from the usual pattern.

clue.text: Old corgi nun had spruced up for canine contests

parts.note: grey describes old age, as in grey-haired

indicators.note: tidied and rearranged, so the letters of corgi nun had are reordered

explanation.surface: An elderly nun had her corgi groomed for dog shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spruced up' rearranges CORGI NUN HAD to give HOUNDRACING.
explanation.definitionFit: Greyhound racing is the sport of dogs chasing a mechanical hare round a track.

clue.text: Allowing the French time can start to grate

parts.note: le is French for the
a tin is a can

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of grate

explanation.surface: Permitting the French to make tins grind on a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start to' gives G from 'grate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Letting someone do something is permitting it, a straight synonym for giving leave.

clue.text: Vampire, firstly impaled, interred by priest

indicators.note: buried inside the word for priest

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

indicators.note: takes just the opening letter of impaled

explanation.surface: A vampire is staked through and then buried by a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firstly' gives I from 'impaled'; 'interred by' places it inside LAMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamia is a female demon of classical myth who drank the blood of children, a bloodsucker akin to a vampire.

clue.text: Yankee stops fellows travelling up for meeting

indicators.note: the letter plugs a gap, stopping up the other word
in a down clue the word goes upward, so it is read backwards

parts.note: dons are university fellows
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American blocks academics heading north to a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling up' turns DONS into SNOD; 'stops' puts Y inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synod is an assembly of church officials, a formal ecclesiastical gathering.

clue.text: Kindly little man takes rodent into hospital department

parts.note: Ben is a short form of a man's name

indicators.note: the department takes in the rodent, holding it inside

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat
a vole is a small rodent

explanation.surface: A kind little chap brings a vole into a hospital ward.
explanation.definitionFit: Benevolent describes a well-meaning, charitable disposition, a close synonym of kindly as an adjective.

clue.text: Warning enigmatic sea captain rebuffed

indicators.note: pushed back, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: Captain Nemo is the mysterious commander of the Nautilus in Jules Verne

explanation.surface: A mysterious skipper ignores a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign of what is to come, often a portent of trouble.

clue.text: More work's work one placed in out-tray regularly

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the selected letters
taking every other letter of out-tray, starting with the second

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An office scene: work goes into the out-tray, one piece after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes U, T, A from 'out-tray'; OP and I go inside. 'More' is Sir Thomas More, not 'additional', and the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas More wrote Utopia in 1516, describing an imaginary island with an ideal society.

clue.text: Musical group's manager in shock?

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a band is a musical group

explanation.surface: A band's manager is stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like surprise but means a thick head of hair; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A headband for hair keeps a mop in place, managing an unruly thatch.

clue.text: Sometimes no advantage getting round Polish girl?

indicators.note: the outer pieces go round the girl's name

parts.note: gain is advantage or benefit
Wanda is a popular Polish girl's name

explanation.surface: Occasionally there's nothing to be gained by bringing a Polish woman round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like the verb (shine) but is the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and again is an idiom for occasionally, at irregular intervals.

clue.text: Old-fashioned loyalty not hard for left-winger

indicators.note: the letter for hard is excluded

parts.note: troth is an archaic word for faithfulness, as in plighting one's troth
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Old values of faithfulness, softened for a radical.
explanation.definitionFit: Trot is informal shorthand for a Trotskyist, a hard-left socialist.

clue.text: Toy guns now manufactured in Ohioan city

indicators.note: made up anew, so the letters are put together differently

explanation.surface: Toy guns are now produced in a Midwestern industrial town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manufactured' rearranges TOY GUNS NOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Youngstown is a city in northeastern Ohio, once a major steelmaking centre.

clue.text: Scientific investigator left with fragments of china

parts.note: tec is slang for a detective

indicators.note: the word china is broken into pieces and reassembled

explanation.surface: A detective leaves with shards of porcelain to analyse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fragments of' rearranges CHINA into HNICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical relates to applied science or specialist know-how, so it overlaps with scientific.

clue.text: Muslim once acted badly, bringing about complaint

indicators.note: the word for complaint is brought around the other

parts.note: a moan is a grumble or complaint
to ham is to overact, so hammed means acted badly

explanation.surface: Someone once overacted, provoking grumbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' marks the term as dated; it is now considered inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohammedan is an old Western term for a follower of Islam, now regarded as outdated and offensive.

clue.text: It's thought of as keen to involve celebrity in slanderous attacks

indicators.note: the word for attacks takes the celebrity inside

parts.note: mud, as in mud-slinging, is slanderous abuse
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Supposed enthusiasm for dragging a star into a smear campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the simile 'keen as mustard'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'keen as mustard' makes the condiment the proverbial image of eagerness.

clue.text: Wife released from prison society invalidates

indicators.note: the letter for wife is freed from the others

parts.note: Newgate was a notorious London jail

explanation.surface: A spouse let out of jail nullifies a club's rules.
explanation.walkthrough: NEWGATE was a historic prison in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to nullify or cancel out, the same as making something invalid.

clue.text: Head cold not too bad around noon

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: the word for passable goes round the letter for noon

parts.note: OK means passable, not too bad

explanation.surface: A head cold is bearable around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Conk is British slang for the head, or the nose, as in a bump on the conk.

clue.text: Submarine needs anti-rust treatment endlessly

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: underseal is a protective coating sprayed under a car body

explanation.surface: A sub requires constant rust protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the L of UNDERSEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Submarine as an adjective means beneath the surface of the sea, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: American extended period in employment

parts.note: an age is a long stretch of time

explanation.surface: An American spends a long stretch in a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the way something is used, its employment or application.

clue.text: Action from party leaders in informing next generation

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

indicators.note: takes the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A political movement whose leaders are briefing the youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders in' gives I, N, G from 'informing next generation'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing is activity or deed, as in 'that was your doing', so it matches action.

clue.text: Marooned pirate catching mum's assassin

indicators.note: the pirate's name holds the word for mum inside

parts.note: Ben Gunn is the castaway ex-pirate in Treasure Island
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A castaway buccaneer seizes his mother's killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'mum' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunman is an armed criminal, typically one hired to shoot someone, much like an assassin.

clue.text: Starter stolen from hired vehicle's central part

indicators.note: the first letter is taken away from the word that follows

parts.note: taxi's, belonging to a cab

explanation.surface: The starter motor was nicked from a rental car's central section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter stolen from' removes the T of TAXIS (read as taxi's).
explanation.definitionFit: An axis is the central line around which something turns or is arranged.

clue.text: Noble actor is poorly represented in painting

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the word for painting

parts.note: painting is a form of art

indicators.note: badly rendered, so the letters of actor is are muddled

explanation.surface: A noble thespian is shown unflatteringly in a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly represented' shuffles the actor letters, which go 'in' after the second letter of the word for painting.

clue.text: Artist in a way feeding bitterness with idle talk

indicators.note: the pieces are fed into the word for bitterness

RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
gas is chatter

explanation.walkthrough: 'feeding' sends the two short pieces into the word for bitterness; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was the French Impressionist painter famous for his ballet dancers.

clue.text: Country route back from Glenallachie

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards
the letters come from within the single word that follows

explanation.surface: A rural road leads back from a Scottish glen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Glenallachie' backwards and the answer sits inside it. Glenallachie is a Speyside whisky distillery.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane is a narrow road, typically in the countryside.
